dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (日医標準レセプトソフト), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux; uses /var/tmp/ file paths, LINE SEQUENTIAL files, and COPY copybooks typical of the ORCA system
evidence: SELECT PARA-FILE ASSIGN FILE-NAME1 ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL
no EXEC CICS, no EXEC SQL, no COMP-3

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (レセプト) software - hospitalization (入院) medical procedure input subsystem
purpose.summary: This program is the hospitalization (入院) medical procedure input component of the JMA ORCA standard receipt software system. It handles data entry for inpatient medical acts/procedures, manages SPA (screen parameter area) data via flat files, and coordinates with numerous subprograms for calculation, insurance combination checks, and disease name management. It is a large batch/interactive program with extensive flag management, index areas, and copybook inclusions.

notable_features: 92 COPY statements indicating heavy use of shared copybooks
No COMP-3 usage (unusual for mainframe COBOL)
Large PIC X(30000) and PIC X(60000) data records for SPA/parameter passing
Japanese EUC-encoded comments (latin-1 decoded with mojibake)
File paths rooted at /var/tmp/ indicating Linux/Unix runtime
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
verdict.notes: Comments are encoded in Japanese EUC-JP but decoded as latin-1, producing mojibake. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system for Japan. Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of ~459KB (10981 lines total). Dialect is GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL based on Linux file paths and absence of mainframe-specific features.
